'''''Curio talinoides''''', syn. '''''Senecio mandraliscae''''', also known as '''blue straws''', '''blue chalksticks''', '''dassieharpuis''', or '''narrow-leaf chalk sticks''', is a succulent plant of the family [[Asteraceae]] that is native to [[South Africa]].<ref>[https://grassworld.myspecies.info/sites/grassworld.myspecies.info/files/tdwg_geo2.pdf {{aut|Brummitt, R.K.}} 2001. TDGW – World Geographical Scheme for Recording Plant Distributions, 2nd Edition]</ref> The origin of this plant is dubious and it may be a [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]].<ref>[http://www.llifle.com/Encyclopedia/SUCCULENTS/Family/Asteraceae/18206/Curio_talinoides_var._mandraliscae Curio talinoides var. mandraliscae (Tineo) P.V.Heath] by Llifle, The Encyclopedia of Succulents</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Blue Chalksticks -- Senecio.jpg|Leaves of blue chalksticks|140px|thumb|left]]
The bluest of the curio plants, it is about 50 to 70 cm tall with 4.5-9.5 cm long leaves that are thickly and alternately arranged, jammed on the stems, and are set about 0.3-0.5 cm aside. The leaves are linear, rising, sickle shaped and would be narrow at both ends.

Unlike the similar looking ''[[Curio repens]]'', its leaves are much narrower and elongated.<ref>[https://pza.sanbi.org/curio-talinoides Curio talinoides (DC.) P.V.Heath] by PlantZAfrica.com</ref> ''Curio repens'' is also easily distinguished by its shorter, often boat-shaped leaves.<ref>[https://worldofsucculents.com/curio-talinoides-narrow-leaf-chalk-sticks/ ''Curio talinoides''] by World of Succulents</ref> It is also easily confused with ''[[Curio ficoides]]'', which has a similar growth habit. However, the leaves of ''C. talinoides'' are rounded-cylindrical in cross section. In contrast, the leaves of ''C. ficoides'' are usually somewhat knife-like, flattened laterally.<ref>G.Rowley (1994). ''Succulent Compositae: A Grower's Guide to the Succulent Species of Senecio & Othonna''. Strawberry Press. {{ISBN|0912647124}}, 9780912647128</ref>

A hybrid of this and 'repens', known as [[× Curio 'Trident Blue'|Senecio 'Trident Blue']], exists.

==Subspecies and cultivars==
* ''Senecio talinoides'' (DC.) Sch.Bip.: (subsp. talinoides) has finer texture
* ''Senecio talinoides subsp. aizoides'' (DC.) G.D.Rowley: has 2-8 [[capitulum (flower)|capitula]] per [[inflorescence]]
* ''Senecio talinoides subsp. chordifolius'' (Hook.f.) G.D.Rowley: has the longest leaves and is more droopy  
* ''Senecio talinoides f. cristatus'': has a crested form.
* ''Senecio talinoides subsp. cylindricus'' (A.Berger) G.D.Rowley: has cylindrical leaves
* ''Senecio talinoides subsp. mandraliscae'' (Tineo) G.D.Rowley: has short [[Spindle (textiles)|spindle]]-like leaves 5–8 mm (0.2-0.3 in) as long as wide, later elongating.
